content.title: About
content.content: Queso Fresco is a soft, fresh Mexican cheese made from cow’s or goat’s milk. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor and a creamy, crumbly texture similar to cottage cheese or feta. The cheese is sold in small blocks and is typically eaten fresh.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Queso Fresco is a staple in Mexican cuisine, used in tacos, enchiladas, and salads.
The cheese is not aged, which gives it a high moisture content and soft consistency.
Unlike many hard cheeses, Queso Fresco does not melt; it softens slightly when heated.
In Mexico it is often served with lime, salt, and chili.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Queso Fresco provides a good amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The cheese supplies high‑quality dairy protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B2 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: Compared with many aged cheeses, Queso Fresco has a lower fat level, making it suitable for a balanced diet.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fresh milk used to make the cheese may retain live cultures that benefit gut health.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy or lactose may react to Queso Fresco.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The cheese is often salted; those limiting sodium should monitor intake.

items.title: Perishable product
items.content: High moisture makes Queso Fresco quick to spoil; keep it refrigerated and consume within a few days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Queso Fresco can be diced, crumbled into salads, added to tacos, burritos, soups, and casseroles. It is commonly served with lime, fresh cilantro, and chili. The cheese pairs well with avocado, tomatoes, and corn.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Queso Fresco in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. It can be frozen, but the texture will change. Discard any cheese with off‑odors or mold.
